lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read presents some real-world content related to the topic of animals and recycles language students are familiar with.
Look for careful reading and check that students are on task.
[Mime flying a kite, as if you’re struggling against the wind.]  “What am I doing? Yes, I’m flying a kite! Do you like kites? Let’s read about an international kite festival!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers checks students’ comprehension of the text through two multiple choice questions.
Look for correct choices and neat handwriting.
“It’s tricky keeping my kite in the air! Can you help me answer these questions, so it doesn’t crash?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book P.115 p.116 - A Listen and say

details: Listen and say makes students aware of the difference between the /əʊ/ and /uː/ sounds.
Look for attentive listening and correct production of each sound.
“‘Kite’ uses a magic ‘e’ to make a long vowel sound. We’re going to use the magic ‘e’ in all our words today. Listen carefully to what it does to the middle vowel!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

details: This activity further consolidates the distinction between the /əʊ/ and /uː/ sounds in a kinaesthetic way, by getting students to recognise this distinction in a proactive way.
Look for accurate identification of the sound groups and neat colouring.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book P.115 p.116 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point and say reinforces the sound distinctions between the two vowel sounds by prompting students to react to them.
Look for accurate pointing and oral reproduction of the words, and all students actively participating.
“When words sound the same, we say that they ‘rhyme’. Can you say these words? Let’s keep my kite flying by finding some words that rhyme!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book P.115 p.116 - B Trace and match the rhyming words

details: Trace provides controlled written word-level production practice of the sounds, and match the rhyming words trains students to listen and look for the written patterns that create the sounds.
Look for accurate and neat tracing, correct matching.

Heads Up:

Heads Down:
